Why Choose Us?
Our school is a place of inspirational learning at the heart of a community where everyone is valued, respected and challenged; providing opportunities for all to learn, grow and thrive together; succeeding today and in the future. In November 2017, Ofsted judged us as 'Good' in all categories and a Section 8 review in 2023 found we had remained a 'Good' school. As the Lead Inspector put it, “this is clearly a great school, on its way to being an excellent school”.

Testimonials
In our school, we follow CARES (Community, Accountability, Resilience, Empowerment, and Sisterhood) which has helped create a welcoming atmosphere for us students. This helps us thrive as a school and makes for a more positive learning environment.
I love how the school always makes you feel welcome, no matter where you are. The community at CHSG is amazing—most people are so friendly, and the staff are just as welcoming! I will always appreciate the wide range of opportunities we are offered.
What I enjoy most about being part of the CHSG community is the wide range of opportunities we’re given throughout the years – from career-focused events to leadership roles. These experiences have helped me grow both personally and academically.
In today’s world, values like empowerment and resilience are so important, especially for young women, and CHSG really focuses on building those. We’re always encouraged to challenge ourselves, but there’s also the support we need to grow from those challenges.
Being at CHSG has helped me grow, not just through my studies, but also through the diversity work I’ve been involved in, including attending summits through the Sutton Youth Board. I’ve loved contributing, being part of initiatives, and making a difference in our school community.

About Us
Headteacher’s welcome
Welcome to Carshalton High School for Girls, also known as Carshalton Girls or ‘Car Girls’. We are an all-girls secondary school with a thriving Sixth Form. We are part of the Girls’ Learning Trust alongside Nonsuch High School for Girls & Wallington High School for Girls, with whom we share longstanding expertise and passion for girls-only education.
You will notice on these pages the clear emphasis we put on serving our community and creating a strong sense of belonging for all of our girls. Our value of ‘sisterhood’ demonstrates just how important this sense of togetherness is, and I judge the overall success of the school on what we achieve as a community.
We are hugely ambitious – for our site, our staff, our sporting & dance achievements, our exam results - and most importantly our students’ futures.
Our motto is ‘Be your best’. We know that there is no one single yardstick for what excellence entails. Instead, we build a safe, compassionate and high-challenge environment in which students are expected and supported to always be their best, whatever that is. Success naturally follows.
To enable this, we prioritise knowing our students. We take the time to get to know every child, using our bespoke pastoral curriculum to develop wellbeing and resilience and push the girls outside of their comfort zone into the sweet spot of growth and achievement. Our very extensive Enrichment programme – from clubs to residential trips – is carefully designed with this philosophy of personal growth in mind.
Our excellent teaching and support staff are, of course, the heartbeat of the school. Leaders here work restlessly to ensure that we have the positive and enjoyable working environment in which our staff can also grow and develop in their own careers.
I invite you to explore our website and discover more about our wonderful school. If you have any questions or would like further information, please do not hesitate to get in touch.
Peter Baumann-Winn Headteacher

Our Motto & Values
Our Motto: Be Your Best
"Be Your Best" is more than just a motto – it’s a mindset. It encourages all students to:
Every student’s best may look different and that diversity is the strength of our community. Whether in the classroom, around school, on the field, or at home, we want every student to feel confident to aim high and set ambitious goals, work hard, and take pride in who she is and what she can achieve.
Focus on progress over perfection
Celebrate their effort, individuality, and growth
Our School Values: CHSG CARES
These values were shaped by input from our whole community. They are the foundation for a culture where students feel seen, supported, and inspired.
Community: We foster kindness, inclusion, and school spirit. We work together, celebrate each other, and create a space where everyone feels they belong.
Accountability: We take ownership of our learning, our behaviour, and our actions. We know that responsibility builds trust and helps us grow.
Resilience: We face challenges with determination. Mistakes are part of learning, and we support each other to keep going when things get tough.
Empowerment: We help every student recognise her strengths, believe in her voice, and step into her leadership potential – in big and small ways.
Sisterhood: We stand by each other. We show empathy, compassion, and encouragement – lifting each other up and celebrating our successes together.
At Carshalton Girls, we are building more than academic success – we are shaping confident, compassionate, and courageous young people who believe in themselves and each other. Our motto and values guide each student every day, reminding her that she is supported, she is capable, and she is enough – just as she is – while encouraging her to grow, learn, and become her best self.

Welcome to CHSG Sixth Form
At Carshalton Girls’ Sixth Form, we believe every student has the potential to excel. Our Key Stage 5 provision is designed to inspire, challenge and support you so that you can achieve your very best – both academically and personally.
Choosing CHSG means joining a thriving, inclusive community where:
You’re known and supported. Our expert staff understand your ambitions and work with you to achieve them.
High expectations drive success. We foster a culture of excellence and aspiration.
Opportunities are everywhere. From personalised guidance to enrichment activities, you’ll have the tools to grow and thrive.
Life beyond the classroom. Our wide range of extracurricular opportunities enrich your experience and broaden your horizons.
We hold the keys to unlocking potential and work closely with every student to ensure success – in the classroom and beyond.
Why Choose CHSG Sixth Form?
Whether you’re continuing from Year 11 at CHSG or joining us from another school, our Sixth Form is an integral and valued part of our school community. Here you’ll:
Develop leadership skills through exciting opportunities.
Pursue new interests and hobbies alongside your studies.
Receive outstanding guidance for your post-18 pathway, including university, apprenticeships, or employment.
Our students consistently tell us how supported and empowered they feel. As Sofya V, one of our Sixth Formers, shares:
“CHSG is a very positive and friendly environment. Teachers believe in me and support my ambitions. The Sixth Form team has guided me through my post-18 options and offered incredible opportunities, like the UCAS Discovery trip to ExCeL.”
Mrs B Norman Director of Sixth Form and Assistant Headteacher
We’re proud of our students’ academic achievements and equally proud of the confidence and independence they gain here – skills they take with them to university, training, work and beyond.
Join CHSG Sixth Form and be part of a happy, successful, and caring environment where you can truly flourish.
Sixth Form Information Booklet

Pupil Premium
What is the Pupil Premium?
The pupil premium grant is paid to schools for the purpose of increasing the aspirations and attainment of students from disadvantaged backgrounds.
The money the school receives is based on the students who are recorded as being eligible for Free School Meals in the last six years, who are ‘Looked After’ or who have a parent serving in the armed forces.
Nationally, there are gaps in the progress (the amount a student improves whilst at school) and attainment (the final grades achieved) made between pupil premium and non-pupil premium students. The grant is paid to schools to implement strategies to reduce this gap. Detailed strategy and funding information specific to Carshalton Girls can be found in our pupil premium statement.
To find out more about Pupil Premium, please go to the government website:
Department for Education

Careers Education
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance at Carshalton Girls provides a stable careers programme of activities to develop the knowledge and skills needed to make informed decisions about career pathways.
CEIAG at Carshalton Girls is delivered within the Careers curriculum and is integrated into the whole school curriculum. The Careers Programme includes Work Experience, Work Related Learning and Enterprise. The school is committed to providing a comprehensive careers programme that meets these requirements and also fulfils the criteria for the Investor in Careers award and fully meets the Gatsby Benchmarks.
Our Careers Policy gives details of the careers, education information, advice and guidance at Carshalton Girls and how the impact of the programme is measured. The next review for this policy will be in Spring 2027.
Mrs Sylvie Hrouda Careers Coordinator Telephone: 020 8647 8294 Email: shrouda@carshaltongirls.org.uk
Our mission is to give students meaningful encounters with employers and to provide them with information regarding all the pathways that are available to them, not only during their time here with us but for life after Carshalton Girls. Throughout the year, we have a number of opportunities for colleges and training providers to support our careers programme. We would encourage you to contact our careers coordinator if you would like to discuss our careers programme.
At Carshalton Girls, you are entitled to receive a programme of work-related and career-related learning, careers information, advice and guidance designed to help you to understand yourself, know what opportunities are available and to make plans to help you achieve your education and career goals.

Uniform and mobile phone reminders
We would like to thank parents and carers for your continued support in maintaining our high standards of uniform and conduct. Following recent reminders in assemblies, we would be grateful if families could ensure that students are in full and correct uniform and ready for learning.
This includes ensuring that students do not wear:
All of which are not permitted under our uniform policy.
In particular, we would like to remind parents that false nails and nail extensions are not permitted. In addition to not meeting uniform expectations, these present a health and safety risk in subjects such as PE, Art and DT and around a busy school environment more generally. From this half-term onwards, students who arrive wearing nail extensions may be sent home to have them removed before returning to lessons.
We would also like to remind families that mobile phones and other smart devices must not be used anywhere on the school site at any point during the school day. Phones should be in pouches from morning registration and after school until they leave the site.
As part of our commitment to safeguarding wellbeing and maintaining a calm, focused environment for learning, we take smartphone-related issues extremely seriously. Where there is reasonable suspicion that a student has access to or is using a prohibited device in school, searches may take place in line with our Behaviour Policy.
We would also like to remind parents that current Year 7 students will continue with a brick-phone-only policy when they move into Year 8 next year. Students will not begin using pouches until Year 9.
We know that the overwhelming majority of our students take pride in representing the school positively, and we are very grateful for the support of parents and carers in helping us maintain the calm, safe and purposeful environment that all students deserve.
Mrs Crump Assistant Headteacher

Examinations and Performance
Examination Results Summer 2026
Carshalton High School for Girls is proud to celebrate another year of strong GCSE and BTEC outcomes.
Students achieved excellent results across a broad and ambitious curriculum, with nearly a third of all grades awarded at Grades 7-9, the highest figure in the last four years and a third consecutive year of improvement. The school's Average Point Score increased to 5.33, continuing a sustained upward trend and representing the strongest performance over the same period. Overall attainment remained high, with 68% of grades awarded at Grade 5 or above and 81% at Grade 4 or above.
We were particularly pleased to see strong outcomes across many areas of the curriculum, alongside continued success in supporting students from a wide range of backgrounds and starting points. Students with SEND and those with English as an Additional Language achieved some of their strongest outcomes in recent years, reflecting the impact of our inclusive approach and commitment to ensuring every student can thrive.
These results are a testament to the hard work, ambition and resilience of our students, the dedication and expertise of our staff, and the invaluable support provided by parents and carers. We congratulate every member of the Year 11 cohort on their achievements and look forward to seeing them flourish as they move on to the next stage of their education, training and employment.
Headline Performance Measures 2026
To enter the EBacc students must complete the following:
Whilst English, Maths and Science are compulsory, the completion of a language and humanity subject are dependent on students' individual options.
Carshalton High School for Girls are delighted that Year 13 students have once again secured many excellent outcomes across a wide range of subjects and courses.
This year saw an increase in the proportion of A*-A grades, while almost 98% of entries achieved grades A*-E. Achievement in vocational qualifications was particularly strong, with BTEC performance placing within the top quartile nationally.
These outcomes reflect the ambition of our curriculum, the quality of teaching and support provided by staff, and the determination shown by our girls throughout their Sixth Form studies.
We are especially pleased that our girls have secured a wide range of positive destinations and are now preparing for exciting next steps at university, in apprenticeships and in employment. We congratulate all of our Year 13 students on their achievements and look forward to hearing about their future successes.
For results by subject, please see the attachments at the bottom of this page.

Remote Learning
While regular full-time attendance at school is our priority, in exceptional circumstances, the school may need to partially or fully close, resulting in some or all students being unable to attend on-site learning for part or all of the school day. Should this occur, we will notify students and parents/carers via the school website and, if possible, our usual email/text message communication. We will provide as much notice as possible.
During a partial or full closure, we would endeavour to provide remote learning. Communication with students will be through their school Microsoft account and students should regularly check their email for information, guidance and updates.
The school will attempt to make arrangements to deliver suitable education for children with SEND who cannot attend school. The SENDCo will work with parents/carers to develop a plan and make reasonable adjustments where possible.
Remote learning may take the following forms:
Students will complete a series of activities specified by their teacher, working through the materials on their own, including their workbooks.
Live Microsoft Teams lessons
Teachers may conduct full lessons online via Microsoft Teams.
This is a mix of independent study and Teams learning.
For example, teachers may hold brief online sessions via Microsoft Teams at the start of the lesson to provide instructions, key information, and an opportunity for questions before students proceed with independent tasks. Alternatively, teachers may set an activity for students to complete before meeting on Teams to discuss the work and provide feedback.

House System
Welcome to the CHSG House System
The House system is a strong feature of the school and this facilitates girls mixing across year groups, to foster friendly but fierce competition. We want to inspire our girls, highlight potential opportunities, and motivate them to greatness with our termly focus on powerful and influential female role models.
Our aim is to provide every student in the school with the following:
We have four houses:
We have a vertically integrated house structure where students are allocated a house on their first day of Year 7 which then will remain in until they leave in Year 11.
Each tutor group has a House Captain who will act as representatives for their House at house events, help co-ordinate and plan activities and attend House meetings.
Each house is in competition with each other to gain as many House Achievement Points as possible. At the end of every academic year the total points earned by the students of each house (including House Achievement Points) are tallied up and the House with the highest points total wins the coveted House Cup.

School Fund
What is Our School Fund?
Government funding for schools is under significant pressure. Over the past ten years, we have seen a considerable reduction in the amount of money we have to invest in the facilities we provide for our students, and our ability to enrich their experience both within and outside the classroom.
Schools across the country have been hit by rising prices – including massive jumps in our energy bills – and increasing running costs that have not been fully funded by the government.
More than ever before, we are relying on the generous voluntary donations that parents, carers and alumnae contribute to provide the very best for our students.
A key value at Carshalton Girls is Empowerment. Our School Fund gives us additional resources to empower our fantastic students by giving them access to the high quality and aspirational enrichment opportunities that they deserve. Your donations will enable us to go the extra mile and invest in their futures.
Over the past few years, our School Fund has predominately been used to resource students and provide transport to extracurricular activities, including sporting fixtures and cultural trips. It has also been used to improve some of our social spaces.
Over the past few years, our School Fund has predominately been used to resource students and provide transport to extracurricular activities, including sporting fixtures and cultural trips. It has also been used to improve some of our social spaces.
Moving forward, we are asking for regular voluntary donations to enable this added investment to continue, as well as raise funds to support a number of new projects such as:
How much you choose to donate is a personal decision and entirely voluntary. Parents/carers often ask us how much we think is reasonable.
Most parents/carers have traditionally donated around £10 per month via direct debit, although some choose to donate more but it is entirely up to you.
Every pound you give us, no matter the value, helps us deliver exciting and rewarding activities for your children.
Donating money to the School Fund couldn’t be easier. There are three different ways:
ParentPay Donations Page
We have set up a special donation page with our trusted provider, ParentPay, where you can make a one-off card payment.
You do not need a Parent Pay account for this.
Bank Transfer
We are able to receive donations via bank transfer.
Please ensure you use the reference code YEAR / TUTOR GROUP (if known) / FULL NAME OF STUDENT to help us to identify it.
If you choose to donate this way, we are only able to receive Gift Aid if you complete the form below and return it to the School Office.
Account Number: 40840860
Sort Code: 30-98-36
Standing Order
For those who prefer to donate via standing order, we have attached the forms you will need to complete below.
You can return these forms electronically by adding a scanned version of your signature, and then emailing this directly to us: finance@girlslearningtrust.org
Or you can print the forms and return them via the School Office – where we also have hard copies already
As a member of the Girls’ Learning Trust, Carshalton Girls is an exempt charity.
Gift Aid allows UK charities to claim back the basic rate tax already paid on donations by the donor. This means we can claim back from the government on your behalf 25p for every £1 donated, boosting the value of the donation by a quarter.
